title: ETHICS OF DISPENSING AND PRESENTATION OF PHARMACEUTICAL PRODUCT
subject: Special

questions.question: What is the main goal of Good Dispensing Practice?
options: Speed up dispensing in busy shops
questions.explanation: Good Dispensing Practice aims to ensure the safe and accurate delivery of the correct medicine with appropriate information. Profit and speed are not the primary goals.

questions.question: Which is NOT one of the Five Rights of Medication Use?
questions.explanation: The Five Rights include right patient, right drug, right dose, right route, and right time. Right price is not one of them.

questions.question: What is the first main activity in the dispensing process?
questions.explanation: The dispensing process begins with reception and validation of the prescription.

questions.question: During validation, what must be confirmed about the prescriber?
questions.explanation: Validation confirms that the prescriber is legitimate, including the name and registration number.

questions.question: When counting tablets in bulk, use:
questions.explanation: Bulk tablets should be counted using gloves and a clean counting tray or counter to avoid contamination.

questions.question: Who gives administration and dosage information?
questions.explanation: The pharmacist is responsible for giving administration and dosage information to the patient.

questions.question: Which is a legal medication classification?
questions.explanation: Over-the-counter (OTC) is a legal medication classification. Brand and generic are not legal categories in the same sense.

questions.question: The superscription “Rx” represents:
questions.explanation: The superscription Rx stands for recipe, meaning “take thou.”

questions.question: The part stating name and strength is the:
questions.explanation: The inscription is the part of the prescription giving the name and strength of the medicine.

questions.question: The subscription gives:
questions.explanation: The subscription gives directions to the dispenser about compounding or dispensing.

questions.question: A prescription requiring compounding is:
questions.explanation: A prescription requiring compounding is a compound or complex prescription.

questions.question: A narcotic prescription must also contain:
questions.explanation: A narcotic prescription must include additional legal details such as the patient address and registry number.

questions.question: All written or printed package matter is called:
questions.explanation: All written or printed matter on or accompanying a package is called labelling.

questions.question: A key label function is to show:
options: How and when to use product
questions.explanation: A key function of the label is to show how and when to use the product.

questions.question: Label information must be all EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: Label information must be accurate, concise, and legible; it should not be lengthy.

questions.question: Labels should be concise to:
options: Save on printing and paper costs
questions.explanation: Concise labels help avoid patient confusion and improve understanding.

questions.question: A non-medicine liquid needs:
questions.explanation: A non-medicine liquid should carry the warning Not to be taken.

questions.question: A preferred positive warning label is:
questions.explanation: Positive warnings state the intended use. For rectal use only is a positive warning label.

questions.question: A suppository label should say:
questions.explanation: Suppositories are intended for rectal use, so the label should say For rectal use only.

questions.question: “Shake well before use” applies to:
questions.explanation: Suspensions settle on standing and must be shaken well before use to ensure dose uniformity.

questions.question: A bottle label goes:
options: Over the bottle opening and cap
questions.explanation: A bottle label is placed on the front, about one-third down the bottle for visibility.

questions.question: Labels often fail to stick because of:
questions.explanation: Labels fail to adhere on a dirty or greasy surface; the container should be clean and dry.

questions.question: A single prefabricated product is a:
questions.explanation: A single prefabricated product corresponds to a simple prescription.

questions.question: “M. et ft. sol. Disp vi” means:
questions.explanation: The abbreviation means mix and make a solution; dispense six.

questions.question: “gtt. iii a.u. hs” means:
options: Three tablets in both ears at bedtime
Three drops in both ears at bedtime
Three grams to affected area after meals
Three drops by mouth every hour
questions.explanation: gtt = drops, a.u. = both ears, hs = at bedtime, so it means three drops in both ears at bedtime.

questions.question: Which is NOT a prescription component?
questions.explanation: A prescription includes prescriber signature, patient details, and date. Pharmacy profit margin is not a prescription component.

questions.question: An official label is used when the formula is:
questions.explanation: An official label is used when the formula appears in a standard reference book such as a pharmacopoeia.

questions.question: An unofficial label is used when the formula is:
questions.explanation: An unofficial label is used when the formula is not in a standard reference.

questions.question: Which is legally required on dispensed medicine labels?
options: Keep out of reach of children
questions.explanation: Among the listed items, the pharmacy name and address is legally required on dispensed medicine labels.

questions.question: “b.i.d.” means:
questions.explanation: b.i.d. means bis in die, twice a day.

questions.question: “p.r.n.” means:
questions.explanation: p.r.n. means pro re nata, as needed.

questions.question: “p.o.” means:
questions.explanation: p.o. means per os, by mouth.

questions.question: Dispensing decisions are based on:
options: Patient’s ability to pay for drugs
questions.explanation: Dispensing decisions are based on prescription validation, not ability to pay, reputation, or stock alone.

questions.question: If an interaction is suspected, the pharmacist should:
questions.explanation: If an interaction is suspected, the pharmacist should consult the prescriber before dispensing.

questions.question: Which is a dosage form instruction?
questions.explanation: Chew it thoroughly is an instruction related to the dosage form. The others concern administration timing, storage, or route.

questions.question: Confidentiality is maintained to:
questions.explanation: Confidentiality is maintained primarily to respect patient privacy.

questions.question: The signa gives directions to the:
questions.explanation: The signa gives directions to the patient on how to take the medicine.

questions.question: Which means “before meals”?
questions.explanation: a.c. means ante cibum, before meals.

questions.question: A hospital medication order form is an:
questions.explanation: A hospital medication order form is an in-patient prescription.

questions.question: Carton labels go on the large side to:
questions.explanation: Carton labels are placed on the large side to keep all information visible.

questions.question: Clean the outside of a container:
questions.explanation: The outside of the container should be cleaned before affixing the label so it adheres properly.

questions.question: “a.u.” refers to:
questions.explanation: a.u. means auris utraque, both ears.

questions.question: Drowsiness warnings apply to:
questions.explanation: Drowsiness warnings are important for sedatives and other central nervous system depressants.

questions.question: Too much label information may cause:
questions.explanation: Too much label information may cause patient confusion, so labels should be concise.

questions.question: An external preparation label should say:
questions.explanation: An external preparation should be labelled For external use only.

questions.question: An inhalation preparation may be labelled:
questions.explanation: An inhalation preparation may carry the warning Not to be taken orally.

questions.question: “q.s.” means:
questions.explanation: q.s. means quantum sufficit, sufficient quantity.
